runtime-info.title: Runtime metrics guide
runtime-info.subtitle: What every number on a runtime card actually means
runtime-info.intro: Each card shows a live snapshot of a single <highlight>Exodus process</highlight>. Use this guide to understand what each metric measures and when to worry about it.
runtime-info.instance-types-description: Exodus is split into several specialized processes. Each one has its own job, its own memory, and its own event loop.
runtime-info.api-description: Handles every HTTP request from the dashboard and subscription endpoints. This is the <highlight>main user-facing process</highlight> — virtually every panel and subscription request is served here.
runtime-info.scheduler-description: A <highlight>cron-driven dispatcher</highlight>. It does not run any work itself — at the scheduled moment it simply pushes a job into the queue for the <highlight>Processor</highlight> to pick up.
runtime-info.processor-description: The actual <highlight>worker</highlight>. It consumes queued jobs and runs the heavy lifting: <highlight>node health checks</highlight>, <highlight>traffic aggregation</highlight> per user and per node, and other long-running tasks that must not block the API.
runtime-info.memory-description: Where the process holds its working data. All values are reported by Node.js in real time.
runtime-info.heap-description: Memory used by JavaScript objects, managed by <highlight>V8</highlight> — the Node.js engine. Shown as <highlight>used / total</highlight>. A high ratio is <highlight>expected and healthy</highlight> — V8 holds onto memory until it really needs more, so something like <highlight>100 / 120 MB</highlight> is normal, not a warning.
runtime-info.rss-description: <highlight>Resident Set Size</highlight> — the total physical memory the OS has given to the process, including the heap, native code, and shared libraries. The best single signal of <highlight>how much RAM this process is actually using</highlight>.
runtime-info.external-description: Memory held outside V8 by native C++ objects bound to JavaScript — typical sources are <highlight>open sockets</highlight>, <highlight>streams</highlight>, and Buffer-backed payloads.
runtime-info.array-buffers-description: Memory specifically allocated for <highlight>ArrayBuffer</highlight> and <highlight>Buffer</highlight> instances (raw binary data). It is counted as a subset of <highlight>External</highlight>.
runtime-info.event-loop-description: Health of the single-threaded loop that drives all asynchronous work in Node.js. If the loop is blocked, the whole process stalls.
runtime-info.delay-description: Average time between consecutive event loop ticks. A healthy value sits close to <highlight>0–2 ms</highlight>. Higher numbers mean the loop is being blocked by long synchronous work.
runtime-info.p99-description: <highlight>99th percentile</highlight> of event loop delay over the measurement window. Reveals worst-case latency that the average alone hides — useful for spotting occasional spikes.
runtime-info.active-handles-description: Long-lived resources keeping the loop alive: <highlight>open sockets</highlight>, <highlight>timers</highlight>, <highlight>file descriptors</highlight>. A steady state is normal; <highlight>unbounded growth</highlight> is a strong leak signal.
runtime-info.threads-description: OS threads used by the Go process. This normally changes with blocking syscalls, cgo, and scheduler decisions.

info.title: How usage is calculated
info.summary: Returns internal squad members who spent at least the given threshold over the selected period, with the total volume for each of them.
info.nodes-intro: A squad isn't tied to nodes directly — the link is derived through inbounds:
info.nodes-step-1: All inbounds that belong to the internal squad are taken.
info.nodes-step-2: For each inbound, the config profiles it belongs to are resolved.
info.nodes-step-3: A node is counted when it has such a profile set as active and that inbound is enabled on the node itself.
info.nodes-outro: So only the nodes a squad member can <hl>actually connect to right now</hl> are counted. If the squad has no inbound available on at least one node, the list is empty.
info.traffic-granularity: Stats are stored with daily granularity: one record = user + node + day. Node data is flushed to the database roughly every 2 minutes, so today's numbers are near real-time, lagging by up to a couple of minutes.
info.traffic-sum: For each member, all of their daily per-node records are summed over the period from the start of start to the end of end (both dates inclusive, UTC).
info.traffic-threshold: Only users whose total is ≥ minTotalBytes make it into the response. Volume is returned in raw bytes, without rounding.
info.caveats-per-node: Traffic is counted per whole node, not per inbound. If a node is shared across squads (its active profile also serves other inbounds), the user's total includes all their traffic on that node — including what they poured through other squads' inbounds. It's an upper bound, not exact per-squad attribution.
info.caveats-membership: Squad membership and the node set are taken at request time, not historically. A user who left the squad disappears from the response (even though they used traffic); a recently joined one shows all their traffic for the period, including days before joining. The same goes for a change of a node's active profile.
info.caveats-sorting: The list is sorted by user ID, not by volume. Since traffic changes in real time, data may drift between pages — to hunt down abusers, set a minTotalBytes threshold instead of reading everyone.

node-ssh.title: SSH terminal
node-ssh.key-description-imported: Signing uses the key you imported; it never leaves your browser. Make sure its public half is in authorized_keys on the server.
node-ssh.key-import-description: Stays in this browser, encrypted in the vault. Passphrase-protected keys are not supported.

key-error.encrypted: This key is passphrase-protected. Remove the passphrase, or import a copy without one.
key-error.malformed: The key could not be read. Copy the whole file, including the BEGIN and END lines.
key-error.unsupported-algo: Only Ed25519 and RSA keys are supported.
key-error.unsupported-format: That does not look like a private key file.

node-ssh.seed-warning: Write these 12 words down and keep them offline. They are the only way to restore your SSH keys — the panel never sees them and cannot recover them for you.
node-ssh.unlock-description: Enter the 12 words you saved when the vault was created.
node-ssh.seed-invalid: This is not a valid 12-word recovery phrase
node-ssh.seed-mismatch: This phrase does not match the vault stored in this browser
node-ssh.key-description: A dedicated key was generated for this node and never leaves your browser. Add the line below to authorized_keys on the server, then connect.
node-ssh.host-hint: Leave empty to use the node address
node-ssh.hostkey-new-description: This is the first time you connect to this host from this browser. Verify the fingerprint out of band before trusting it.
node-ssh.hostkey-changed-description: The host key does not match the one you trusted earlier. This can mean the server was reinstalled — or that someone is intercepting the connection.
node-ssh.passcode-required-description: The vault cannot be used in this browser until you set a passcode. It also saves you from typing the recovery phrase every time.
node-ssh.passcode-title: Set a passcode for this browser
node-ssh.passcode-description: Unlocks the vault on this browser after a reload.
node-ssh.passcode-length: {{length}} characters, at least one of them a letter.
node-ssh.passcode-unlock-description: Enter the passcode you set for this browser.
node-ssh.passcode-exhausted: Too many wrong attempts, the passcode was turned off. Unlock with your recovery phrase and set a new one.
node-ssh.ticket-failed: The panel refused to open a session.
node-ssh.export-locked: Unlock the vault first — a backup can only be made from an open vault.
node-ssh.export-description: Saves an encrypted file with your node keys and addresses. Nothing in it is readable without the recovery phrase, so it is safe to keep anywhere.
node-ssh.import-description: Restores keys from a backup file. Enter the recovery phrase that the backup was created with.
node-ssh.import-invalid: This file is not a vault backup
node-ssh.import-mismatch: The recovery phrase does not open this backup
node-ssh.reset-description: Deletes the vault and every SSH key in it. The private keys are gone for good, so the public keys already installed on your nodes become useless and you will have to install a new one on each. Panel access is not affected.
node-ssh.lost-everything: Lost both the passcode and the phrase?
